Hello everyone,

I'm new to this forum. My name's Lyz and I am currently a 3d animation and film student at Virginia Commonwealth University in Virginia. I have been interested in holograms ever since middle school; they have been a fascination of mine. I have realized in my own holographic research that the next step in entertainment is to develop 3D holographic media. I am posting in order to develop a conversation with those who are also interested in the development of three dimensional television, whether you study holography at institutes, or are also fascinated with holography as I am. 

If I am able to keep contact with like-minded people, I offer my services as a computer animation artist in order to give 3D holography the appearance and presentation it deserves. I hope to hear from you.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
There are lots of problems with 3-D moving media. One is the large amount of information involved. The other is point of view. There are many solutions to all of these problems but none have solved them all well enough to become a standard.

You will want to look a Liti holographics site as they can take a few seconds of your animation and turn it into a hologram for you. These are actually stereograms that contain a few hundred images. Some search terms are multiplexed hologram, holographic stereogram, autostereoscopic. There are many 3-D technologies out there. Dinesh is up on many of them. One time I went to his house and we made a 3-D video of he and I brewing.

You will also want to look at MIT media labs web site for there holovideo project. 

If you think of one of the problems, to start, if we made a hologram the size of a movie screen and fillled an audience, the experience would be different for people sitting in different seats. On the left side of the theater you would see one profile of Gene Harlow and in the middle you would see her head on.

Now making a very long film of a stereoscopic hologram would be actually pretty easy, in film budget terms. If we wanted to make a 6x8 foot feature length movie and had a 20 million dollar budget it would not be terribly difficult. The technology of motion control developed for the first Star Wars film is equal in complexity.

Well, there is a start you are at the beginning of a long road. Welcome aboard!

posts.author: Steve
posts.content_md:
I've been playing with 3D animation for a wile also [http://mywebpages.comcast.net/S.M.Animation/](http://mywebpages.comcast.net/S.M.Animation/)

I've been looking into doing computer generated animated holograms. Basically a multiplexed hologram done all in the computer and printed on a laser printer. So far I haven't even gotten still images I'm happy with. I'll play with it for a while more and see what comes of things. Over all it looks like there is only about 5% the resolution needed in print format and I'll probably need to shoot the images to film. 

Another thing you might look at is Lenticular images. Not really holograms, but a step in the direction of 3D images. Guess the dream of 3D film is the feeling you get of being there at a live production and the ability to include FX work or animated things you can only do to film.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
A few years ago, I worked on a system in which the screen is a hologram optical element and regular video projectors were the source. There is one projector for each eye, so a single viewer sees 3-D without the need for any glasses. The HOE could easily be made for up to six viewers, each having allowable head movement of approximately +/- 3" horizontally and vertically.

The system could theoretically be used with 50 projectors (if they were small enough) so that viewers sitting anywhere along a horizontal line in front of it would see an autostereoscopic image3-D image, dependant upon their perspective view. In the first case, two cameras were needed for recording the scenes. In the second, 50 cameras would be needed. 

The big problem with *any* 3-D system is the availability of adequate and appropriate content along with the release of the system. I can make a 3-D TV, what value does it give to those watching soap operas, newstainment, advertisements, censored movies, or infomercials?

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
3D TV and 3D autostereo displays are not that uncommon. Edwina Orr and David Traynor of Richmond studios designed and buiilt a pretty impressive one. The German comapny DDD ( [http://www.ddd.com/](http://www.ddd.com/) ) has also got a pretty impressive one. They (DDD) demo it at the SPIE 3D conference (sadly moved to the week before "holography" this year ) You might also try to find and go to the NSA ( [http://www.stereoview.org/](http://www.stereoview.org/) ) conferences where you'll see lots and lots of autostereo!

We (Triple take holographics) have done lenticulars from computer generated images, mostly from Bryce and they work pretty well. If you want to see those, just email me and I'll send a stereo pic of some.

I think the "value" of 3D is in the eye of the beholder. I think we may be imposing our cultural (or "gasp!" intellectual) values onto the public. It seems almost de rigeur to pooh pooh soap operas (I've never watched one - Not even "Coronation Street" ). However, our society is propelled by money and people spend money on all sorts of stuff that we might think is stupid. I remember a quote in the early days of the telelphone where someone asks, "Why would I want to talk to someone many miles away. If I did, I'd just visit them" Or words to that effect. Money for major scientific breakthroughs often come from commercial interests. These commercial interests must make enough money to be able fund pure research. Thus the talking chihuahuas, the frazzled college student, the perpetual heartburn etc etc. If a few gazillion people watch Coronation Street and maybe a few thousand (if that!) watch "Physics For The People, Part XX - Quantum Electrodynamics" Watch as <well known TV Presenter> fumbles through an amazing explanation for the layman on this amazing aspect of a theory that makes amazing predictions and shows amazing insights into the Universe. Is God passe? Watch "Physics For the People, PartXX _Quantum Electrodynamics"! Tonight on Channel <some "scientific channel"> . I think most big commercial interest will put their money into sponsoring the soap!

A drop of a few percentage points on the Dow could wipe out entire university chairs!
